discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single electron spins in diamond (NV centres) and their use as room-temperature quantum sensors
motivation: Wrachtrup and Jelezko first optically detected and coherently manipulated a single electron spin in a solid at room temperature, using the nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond. They also demonstrated entanglement with nearby nuclear spins and single-shot readout. Lukin, together with these pioneers, proposed and demonstrated that a single NV spin works as a nanoscale magnetometer of unprecedented sensitivity and spatial resolution. Together they turned a single quantum system into a dependable measurement instrument. Today NV sensors image magnetism in 2D materials and superconductors, detect nuclear magnetic resonance from nanolitre volumes, map neuronal and geological fields, and work inside diamond anvil cells beyond 100 GPa. Their work joined fundamental quantum control of individual spins to a broadly used new measurement capability, linking quantum optics, condensed-matter physics, materials science and biology.
